skill.name: iterative-runner
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through bounded retry loops until tests pass, lint errors are fixed, or completion criteria are met.
skill.summary: Run bounded AI coding iterations until defined success criteria are met.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: The main real risk is that the skill demonstrates repeated agent execution through shell commands, including one unbounded loop example. Most static findings are Markdown fence or inline-code false positives, and I found no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the core infinite loop example with a bounded command that uses --max-iterations and a clear stop condition.
Warn users to run iterative commands only in trusted repositories with clean version control and reviewed prompts.
Label command blocks as examples and keep non-command prompt templates outside bash-style fences.

content.value_statement: Long coding tasks often fail because tests, lint checks, or completion criteria are not retried consistently. This skill provides a bounded loop pattern for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides a retry-loop workflow for AI-assisted coding tasks.
Shows how to define completion promises and success criteria.
Recommends max-iteration limits to reduce runaway loops.
Supports TDD-style cycles that write tests, implement fixes, and rerun checks.
Includes a reusable prompt template for feature implementation loops.
limitations: Does not include an executable runner script in this package.
Requires users to supply safe prompts, tests, and stop criteria.
May repeat mistakes if the underlying agent lacks new feedback.
Can consume compute or API quota during long runs.

use_cases.title: TDD Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to keep retrying fixes until tests pass or a bounded iteration limit is reached.

use_cases.title: Overnight Build Recovery
use_cases.description: Run a controlled agent loop that attempts build repairs and reports blockers when the limit is reached.

use_cases.title: Flaky Task Retrying
use_cases.description: Give teams a repeatable pattern for complex tasks that need several repair and verification cycles.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Test Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterative-runner to fix the failing test. Stop when all tests pass. Use a maximum of 10 iterations.

prompt_templates.title: Define Completion Criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the requested feature. Treat all tests passing and no linter errors as completion. Output the completion marker only after verification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the feature with TDD. First add a failing test, then implement, run checks, and revise within 25 iterations.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Bounded Multi-Phase Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an iterative loop for this migration. Complete schema changes, tests, and documentation in phases. After 30 failed iterations, summarize blockers.

output_examples.input: Fix a failing unit test with a 10 iteration limit.
output_examples.output: The agent describes each attempt, applies focused changes, reruns the test, and stops when the suite passes.

output_examples.input: Implement a feature using TDD completion criteria.
output_examples.output: The agent reports added tests, implementation changes, verification results, and a final completion marker.

output_examples.input: Continue an overnight build until a bounded success condition.
output_examples.output: The workflow records attempts, stops at the maximum iteration count, and lists blockers if success is not reached.

best_practices: Set a maximum iteration count before starting any loop.
Define observable success criteria such as tests passing or lint checks passing.
Review prompts and repository state before allowing repeated agent actions.
anti_patterns: Running an unbounded loop without a stop condition.
Using vague completion criteria such as done or looks good.
Pointing the loop at secrets, production systems, or unreviewed prompts.

faq.question: Does this skill run code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples. Users decide whether to run any command.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude and can inform Codex or Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Why should I set max iterations?
faq.answer: A limit prevents runaway loops, quota waste, and repeated unwanted changes.

faq.question: Can it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. Review code changes, test results, and failure summaries before merging.

faq.question: What completion criteria work best?
faq.answer: Use measurable checks, such as tests passing, lint passing, or a specific completion marker.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: Use it only with careful review and safe environments. Avoid direct changes to production resources.
